synthetic_power_comparison.notes: Main claim (paper Fig. 1B regime): n_M=100, n_J=10,000, alpha=0.25, zeta=0.05, informative judge, true failure rate 0.20. Instances are generated by the evaluator; every instance draws its own judge TPR/FPR within +/-0.03 of the regime centre (train: the paper's 0.95/0.05; hidden test: a nearby centre with the same TPR-FPR). The results below are the values recorded from the paper's synthetic figure and are unchanged.

type2_error.description: Rate of failing to certify a genuinely reliable model (true failure rate 0.20 < alpha) with an informative judge.

synthetic_type2_curve.notes: Mean Type-II error over true failure rates {0.01, 0.15, 0.175, 0.225} with the informative judge. The paper shows these curves only graphically (Fig. 1/11, parametrised by alpha at R_M=0.25), so the results here are this gym's reference-run values on the public train slice, not paper numbers. The 0.01 cell probes rare failures (the paper's stated limitation: normal approximations with rare failure events).

type2_error.description: Mean rate of failing to certify a reliable model across failure rates from very safe to just below the threshold.

judge_quality_sweep.notes: Mean Type-II error over two less reliable judges (paper Fig. 1A: TPR 0.75/FPR 0.05, Fig. 1C: TPR 0.95/FPR 0.25; hidden test: nearby centres with the same TPR-FPR) at true failure rates {0.05, 0.15, 0.20}. The paper reports (Theorem 5.4, Fig. 1A/1C) that the noisy test does not beat the human-label-only test with such judges; this experiment measures where the paper's method falls short. Results are this gym's reference-run values on the public train slice.

type2_error.description: Mean rate of failing to certify a reliable model when the judge misses failures or raises false alarms.

oracle_gap.notes: Gap between a method's mean Type-II error and the known-judge reference test's, averaged over all eleven alternative cells (main, curve and sweep). The known-judge row is computed by the evaluator with each instance's true judge TPR/FPR. Previously recorded single-cell value: noisy_ht oracle_gap 0.33 at the main cell (kept under _previous_results). Results are this gym's reference-run values on the public train slice.

oracle_gap.description: Mean Type-II error minus that of the known-judge reference test on the same instances: the cost of not knowing the judge's reliability.

mean_type2_error.description: Mean Type-II error over the same cells (reported only; it equals oracle_gap plus a constant fixed by the evaluator).

synthetic_type1_control.notes: Validity is enforced as a hard gate by the evaluators, not rewarded: in every judge regime the false-certification rate at the null boundary (R_M=alpha, 3,000 instances) and inside the null (1,000 instances) must not exceed zeta + 0.015 = 0.065, otherwise the certifier's run is scored as failed (all scored metrics at their worst value, non-zero exit). These metrics are reported with coefficient 0 so that being more conservative than required is not rewarded. type1_error is the informative-judge regime; the values below are the figure/Monte Carlo approximations recorded for that panel and are unchanged.

type1_error.description: False certification rate at the null boundary with the informative judge (validity; gated, not rewarded).

type1_error_worst_regime.description: Largest null-boundary false certification rate across the three judge regimes (gated, not rewarded).

false_cert_interior.description: Largest false certification rate for clearly unreliable models (true failure rate above alpha) across regimes (gated, not rewarded).
